The latest batch of updates to Voat includes a new CSS class on the body element, to indicate if the user is using the light or dark base stylesheet.

The light stylesheet is what you see by default or when you're not logged in. The dark stylesheet is loaded when you enable night mode.

As an example, this is how you might style links differently for night mode:

a {
 color: #4AABE7;
 text-decoration: none;
}

.dark a {
 color: #967AFF;
}

You can also target the light theme specifically, if you only want to change an element for users not on night mode:

.light a {
 color: #4AABE7;
}

Here's the pull request that added this feature.
[Tip] You can now target night mode users with CSS

Hm. Probably not the greatest idea, but you could add .light to the front of every rule in your custom CSS. This would cause each rule to only apply when the user is not in night mode.

Effectively, in normal mode you'll see Typogra; in night mode, you'll see the default dark stylesheet without any of Typogra's rules.

It has been almost a year since I've LD'd. I never had to try before, it just happened. I've tried to learn the techniques but I get frustrated with anticipation then wake up not being able to sleep. I miss it but it's weird that it keeps me up at night if I try. Any suggestions are welcome.
Haven't had a LD in a really long time.

Keep reading up on it. Going through this subverse or going onto Dreamviews and reading things will help you be thinking about lucid dreaming. I guess that's how I did it, I just kept reading about it and trying techniques. It puts it into your mind and if you think about it during the day, it will almost certainly pop into your mind in your dreams.

Almost all of my LDs have been DILDs (Dream Induced Lucid Dreaming dreams) but if you have a technique that you want to try, give it a go and don't give up if it doesn't work the first few times.

I also kept a dream journal but it has probably been a year since I've written an entry. Sometimes I also wake up in the middle of the night, go to the bathroom and have a drink from the tap and then when I'm ready to stay still or try a technique, I just want to go back to sleep. Fight this urge if you want to LD because it requires practice, just like riding a bike or learning a programming language does.

If you're the sort of person who likes to wake up in the middle of the night to try induce lucid dreaming, try the WBTB (Wake Back to Bed) technique.

As a teenager, I weighed close to 200 pounds. Unhappy with my body,and the size 14 pants I had to buy, I decided to lose weight. I picked up a passion for a sport and started to watch what I ate. Through slow, subtle changes I lost 55 pounds by sophomore year of college. My weight plateaued at 145 lbs for about two years. A change in colleges reignited my desire to lose weight. After not having much success with cardio alone, I started strong lifts. One of my biggest regrets is not taking good pictures before I started lifting! In October, I transitioned to ICF 5x5. http://i.imgur.com/R7FCn8k.jpg http://i.imgur.com/hh6OSWP.jpg

For months, my weight continued to hover around 145lbs. It didn't bother me very much because I saw LOTS of improvement as my body changed from fat to muscle. I went from a size 9 to a size 5, and noticed graceful muscles replacing sloppy, floppy fat. It took me a long time to stop weighing myself daily and start counting calories. My disordered eating as a teenager made counting calories a VERY slippery slope at first. It was hard not to obsess over what I ate, and avoid falling back in to a starvation and binge cycle. In the past three months after making numerous changes to my emotional well being, I started to count calories. It's really been in the past three months that I've lost these 15 pounds, which I attribute to my focus on diet and sticking with a weight training program that I like.

http://i.imgur.com/P9c4VnJ.jpg http://i.imgur.com/1k4xwZG.jpg http://i.imgur.com/OXcmaM9.jpg http://i.imgur.com/Rpdq47V.jpg current stats: weight 130lbs bench: 80lbs squat: 120lbs DL: 155 lbs

My stats are on the lower side as I'm quite injury prone, and have preexisting musculoskeletal injuries.

It's been a long journey, but it's far from over. I've done a really great job maintaining my weight and worked hard to overcome my disordered eating. I eat between 1400-1700kcal a day. My goal is about 1600kcal a day, a deficit from my TDEE. I still want to loose about 5-8 more pounds this summer before a winter bulk. This is the happiest I have ever been with my body, and I'm enjoying creating a loving relationship with it.
